To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of binary kernel discrimination depends crucially on the quality of the training set and on the method that is used to determine the optimal value of its only parameter.

(i) BKD is a useful method for virtual screening of large compound databases; (ii) the predictive power of this method is dependent on the quality of the training set; (iii) the best results are achieved when the training set is free of false positives, i.e., the molecules in the training set that are incorrectly classified as active compounds; (iv) the best results can be achieved by optimizing the smoothing parameter in a particular manner; (v) the best results were achieved using

the optimal value for the smoothing parameter is dependent on the number and type of false positives in training set and the best results are obtained by using one particular optimization procedure for the determination of this parameter and one particular kernel function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of BKD for virtual screening.
the development of new methods to analyze and interpret the results obtained from virtual screening.
the development of a new virtual screening tool for drug discovery, and the results show that the method can be a useful tool in this area.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the best results are achieved when the optimization method used to determine the smoothing parameter is the method of steepest descent, and the kernel function is Jaccard/Tanimoto, and the training set is as free of false positives as possible.
the best performance is obtained by using the optimization method that was used in the present paper and by using the Jaccarad/Tanimoto coefficient for the kernel function.
BKD is not a good choice for virtual screening, and that the results presented here are not a recommendation of the method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BKD, when applied to the MDL Drug Database, is a useful tool that is able to predict the activity of compounds in a test set with a high degree of accuracy.
, when applied to the MDL Drug Database Report, BKD can be made to perform as well as the more computationally expensive support vector machine (SVM) method.
the performance of BKD can be optimized by careful selection of the training data and the use of an appropriate optimization method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BKD, as with any machine learning method, is only as good as the data that are used in its construction.

, in general, the use of a large number of training set compounds does not guarantee that the predictive power of the model produced by BKD will be optimal, as it is the quality of the data, and not the size of the training set, that is crucial.
, for BKD to work well, the training set should be free from false positives and should contain a sufficient number of true positives.
